column1: # Specified by The Designer, Step 1 Wave 2 review section 3.3; accepted by The Manager at the
# Step 1 close, decision 5.2. Built and loaded at sub-step 1.14 by The Engineer.
# quantity-id is written BARE, without brackets, so tools/quantities.js does not read this
# column as a quotation tag. oracle/** is inside the counting rule's declared file set.
#   AMC-1 no two rows with state:owed name the same non-"-" quantity id
#   AMC-2 every superseded-by resolves to a row that is not itself superseded
#   AMC-3 every target is a row in oracle/MANIFEST.tsv
#   AMC-4 no row is applied while its target's manifest row reads specified
#   AMC-5 every pair of owed rows sharing (target, section) is reported. WARN, not FAIL: rows
#         legitimately share a section and only a person can tell a collision from a queue.
# THE AMC- NAMESPACE. Renamed at sub-step 2.19, 2026-08-28, by The Designer. Row AM-143, and
# The Manager's Step 1 close item 24. The checks were AM-1..AM-5 and the rows are AM-01..AM-145:
# one prefix over two closed sets, so a true statement about one read as a statement about the
# other. That ambiguity aggravated a correction against The Systems Engineer.
#   A CHECK id is AMC- plus ONE digit.
#   A ROW id is AM- plus TWO OR MORE digits, zero-padded. The register already wrote AM-01, so
#     no row changes and no author has to remember to pad.
#   THEREFORE: AM- followed by exactly one digit at a word boundary is a DEFECT TOKEN. The test
#     is a grep, not a habit, and it is SCOPED, because unscoped it fires on every document that
#     explains the rename - measured at 2.19, 15 lines of the deliverable and 8 rows here, all of
#     them legitimate mentions. Scope: rows of THIS FILE whose source-substep is 2.19 or later,
#     THE AMC- ALLOWANCE IS NOT A LOOPHOLE. After the boundary the only reason to write a retired
#     name is to say what it became, and a line doing that carries both. Of the ten rows filed at
#     2.19, eight carry no unpadded token and the two that do are the rename itself. The first
#     test passes today. The second cannot pass until AM-144 lands.
#     A register accumulates DATED ROWS, so a file-level date test cannot work on it: this file
#     postdates the boundary and holds rows from R-2, R-3, R-4 and C-1 whose content does not.
#     The source-substep column is the per-row date and the scope uses it.
#   AM- is not a substring of AMC-1, so a grep for row references cannot pick up a check
#     reference, or the reverse. That was not true of the old pair and it is the whole point.
# RETIRED NAMES, which this notice must name in order to retire them. They name the CHECKS in
#   and that reading is fixed by the date. 159 sites carry them. 143 are historical record in
#   files sub-step 2.19 may not edit; rewriting them would make a 2026-08-27 report describe a
#   name that did not exist on 2026-08-27, which is falsifying a record to tidy a namespace.
#   They are correct as they stand and are deliberately not touched.
#   26 live sites remain: tools/check_registers.js (22) and oracle/check_register.md (4).
#   They are AM-144 and AM-145. THE RENAME IS NOT DONE UNTIL THOSE LAND, because the name the
#   tool PRINTS is the name a reader greps for.
# The check list above read four checks from 1.14 until 2.19, and there have been five since
# R-3, when AM-112 was implemented as the fifth. The count is corrected here with the rename.
# oracle/check_register.md CHK-28 carries the same understatement and it is AM-145.

The direction discriminator is defined only where CURRENCY is upstream-ahead; exit 128 is unknown rather than false. --is-ancestor is reflexive and unguarded accuses the author on every equal session.

CONTESTED cannot buy two personas: a register axis may carry any number of sides and truncating to two makes the router choose which sides the user hears. APPLIED AT R-3 as part of the single version-2 edit. Contract section 1: one per side, minimum two, no cap. Suite VRD-7 amended, VRD-9 generalized from a pair to a set. The quantity cell named Q-LCC-SIDES-GT2 (10 of 15 on the Step 0 draft); the warrant that survives is Q-LCC15-SIDES-GT2 (7 of 15 on the authored rows), whose own conditions field reconciles the two. No numeral is carried into the contract: the contract states the rule and the measurement stays in its birth file.

A one_sided axis cannot produce a CONTESTED verdict. APPLIED AT R-3 in the version-2 edit. Contract section 1: CONTESTED fires on class two_sided or false_pair; one_sided produces LITERATURE or BOTH carrying its side and the one-side disclosure at register_schema section 7. Suite VRD-13, LIM-10 and LIM-11 added. The failure it prevents is an unsatisfiable requirement, which fails as a refusal carrying no reason code.

Rule V CONTESTED moves findings from Forbidden to permitted-and-never-counted. APPLIED AT R-3 in the version-2 edit. Rule V gains a FOURTH COLUMN, Permitted-not-counted, because a two-column parser finds findings in neither column, emits the version-1 cell list against the version-2 rules, and returns green. Suite RV-25 flips to legal, RV-35 and RV-36 added, RV-34 retired and replaced by RV-37 which asserts 35 cells and 10 legal.

The misclassified reason code condition is container-shaped and is replaced. APPLIED AT R-3 in the version-2 edit. Owner unchanged and still match_keys. Suite REF-7 and REF-11 amended, REF-18 added as the false-refusal defence.

Landed as ONE edit carrying eleven amendments, per the amended section 9: the integer names a state of the file, not a count of the amendments that produced it. Every trace line whose origin is app names the lsei ref the value was computed against. APPLIED AT R-3 in the version-2 edit. Arity unchanged; the ref rides the locator and the origin function strips it before resolving. Suite TRC-12 added, with a decoy: strip the ref from one app trace and TRC-12 goes red while TRC-3 stays green, because a fixed-arity parser cannot see it.
The ref is read live once per run, git -C lsei rev-parse --short HEAD, never from .oracle-state.json. APPLIED AT R-3 in the version-2 edit, contract section 3.

The live ref is compared against copies.lsei.head; a mismatch is a report line on the answer. APPLIED AT R-3 in the version-2 edit, contract section 3. Stated as a report and NOT a refusal, because the working copy moving mid-session is the drafting assumption A3 doing what it assumes, and a refusal there refuses a working install.

Every run log row records the app ref, or - where lsei was absent. APPLIED AT R-3 in the version-2 edit. Nine fields, closed. Suite LOG-12 amended from eight to nine and LOG-25 added. The column is not recoverable from the traces: a run that emitted no app trace records the ref anyway, and finding every answer computed before lsei moved is one grep over the log against a parse of every deliverable file on disk.

An app trace with no ref is a refusal, reason code input-missing, owner the bootstrap. APPLIED AT R-3 in the version-2 edit, WITH ITS TIMING PINNED, which is the whole content of the change. The refusal fires at the START of the run, when the ref cannot be read, before classification and with zero personas spent. A refusal reached after the wave has run costs more than the answer it replaces and breaks section 5 unconditional zero-persona rule. An app trace missing its ref after a successful read is an emitter defect, not a refusal. Suite REF-20.

DECLINED AT R-3, and the reason is that this row is filed against the wrong target. The finding (1.4-review F14) is that oracle/bootstrap_contract.md section 6 states one availability condition for two verdicts that have different ones. The answer contract Rule V already distinguishes them and always did: LITERATURE requires at least one literature OR findings, CONTESTED requires one literature per side and permits findings without counting it. There is no contract-side change owed. The whole fix is AM-14 on the bootstrap contract. A pair-row written on both sides of a one-sided finding is a defect of this register, not of the contract.

The run-log schema extension is a third bump, to version 3. SUPERSEDED BY AM-66 AT R-3. It is a real CHANGE and not a real BUMP: the extension landed as AM-70 inside the single version-2 edit. The version integer names a state of the file, not a count of the changes that produced it, and section 9 now says so in the rule rather than in a note. This row is the artefact of the ambiguity, and it is the cleanest evidence that the ambiguity was in the rule and not in either author.

DECLINED AT R-3. Minting a quantity id for the contract version integer is the wrong instrument, and the reason is a property of the quantity rather than of the effort. The counting rule class fixed asserts ONE current value and requires every site to agree; live means a value that moves on its own. The version integer is neither: each file legitimately states the version IT was written against, so a Step 0 document reading 1 is correct and would be made wrong by a tag. The two consumers that matter already have a stronger mechanism than the counting rule - VER-1/2/3 and LOG-20 assert agreement at run time and fail when it breaks, which is how this collision surfaced at all. AM-1 blindness is closed by AM-112 instead, which groups owed rows on (target, section) and needs no id.

Q-ROOT-ALLOWANCE names derived-from: Q-PATH-CEILING-259 and no such block exists. M4 reports it as a dangling parent today. Mint the block from the bisection at 1.7 section 8: 259 pass, 260 fail, git 2.55.0.windows.1, core.longpaths unset at all three scopes, OS LongPathsEnabled 0.
